answer: A refundable security bond makes fake identities expensive instead of free. Every agent locks a deposit before it can transact, and the bond unlocks only slowly after a clean history, so reaching the summit with ten thousand fake accounts means ten thousand deposits frozen at once. Peers can prove duplicate behaviour and slash the bond, turning a hollow shell identity into a real loss rather than a free retry. Honest agents earn the deposit back, while a knoll of abandoned accounts simply forfeits its stake to the honest pool.
